data.narrative:
QunaSys, a Series B quantum computing company founded by Tennin Yan, has raised $33M to date. The quantum computing sector includes 11 peer companies (3 public, 8 private), with comparable players including Quantinuum, IonQ, D-Wave Quantum, Rigetti Computing, and Infleqtion.

Valuation analysis relies on a single applicable method due to data constraints. Stage-progression analysis, using the $33M total raised as a proxy for current value and applying a 1.9x multiplier typical for Series B progression, implies a valuation of $63M. A peer-median approach was not applicable; while 6 same-sector peers exist, none qualified within narrow filters (same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier) to support statistically meaningful triangulation; a broader all-sector median would introduce unacceptable methodology bias.

The triangulated range is $53M (low) to $72M (high), with a median of $63M, derived entirely from stage-progression methodology. This range reflects ±15% variance around the median estimate. Key uncertainties include the limited comparable set at this stage within quantum computing—a sector with only three public benchmarks—and the reliance on a single valuation method. Investors should supplement this analysis with proprietary diligence on QunaSys's technical progress, IP position, and capital efficiency relative to named peers.
